title: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow
summary: End-to-end implementation of the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant for server-side web apps.

content.overview: OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework that lets a third-party application obtain limited access to an HTTP service on behalf of a resource owner. The authorization code flow is the recommended grant type for server-side applications.
content.details: Steps: (1) Register the application with the provider to obtain client_id and client_secret. (2) Redirect the user to the provider authorization endpoint with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, and state. (3) The provider redirects back with code and state on the redirect_uri. (4) The server exchanges the code for an access_token (and optionally refresh_token) at the token endpoint, authenticated with client_secret. (5) The access_token is then used in Authorization Bearer headers to call protected APIs.
content.examples: Authorization URL: https://provider.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=abc123&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/callback&scope=read+write&state=xyz. Token exchange: POST /oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code&code=...&redirect_uri=...&client_id=...&client_secret=...
content.caveats: Always use HTTPS. Validate the state parameter to prevent CSRF. Store client_secret server-side only — never embed it in mobile or browser code; use PKCE for public clients instead. Treat refresh tokens as highly sensitive.
